prompt:
USER REVISION — replace all numeric geographic coordinate UI with address/map location UI across these six supply site management design proposals. User instruction: "the users should not see any lat and lon just the map location or the address only".

Keep the corrected cohesive Aqours shell, six screen purposes and Admin-only scope from the accuracy pass. No application implementation. Edit all six screens, do not add unrelated pages.

ABSOLUTE REQUIREMENT: No user-visible latitude/longitude, lat/lon abbreviations, numeric geographic pairs, decimal degrees, degree symbols, WGS84/EPSG jargon, coordinate headings, precision info, coordinate bounds, examples, placeholders or error copy in ANY screen, input, table, sidebar, tooltip, footer or helper text. Internal API coordinate fields remain required but NEVER render them. Do not include hidden technical notes on the UI explaining backend storage. Street address and familiar place names are the location presentation.

1 DIRECTORY: Remove coordinate column entirely. Columns Site name, Address, Last updated, View details. Canonical address labels and street/landmark details are the primary location. Six fixed alphabetic rows; page 1 of 1, "1–6 of 6", default 20. No map necessary in directory. No search/filter/sort/delete/export/bulk actions.
2 ADD SITE: Keep Site name and canonical PSGC cascading address inputs with required street/landmark details. REPLACE geographic coordinates section with "Site location" map picker showing a believable street/topographic map around Adams, Ilocos Norte, Philippines with ONE movable site pin. Use a geographically coherent actual map-like cartographic surface, no satellite or decorative invented sensor overlays. Helper "Select the site's location on the map. Drag the pin to adjust it." Secondary note "The address and map location are selected separately." The map must support proposed click-to-place/drag pin visually; show zoom +/− controls and map attribution. No manual numeric input, no GPS or geocoding, no search field or auto-map-from-address promise. Label selection "Near the old bridge · Adams, Ilocos Norte" when pin chosen, or "Choose a location on the map" if no pin. Primary Create supply site/Cancel.
3 DETAILS: Location presented as full canonical address and a compact read-only map with the selected site pin labelled North Reservoir, Adams, Ilocos Norte. No numeric coordinates anywhere. Keep record ID and created/updated timestamps and Edit site / Back to supply sites. Use the map as the location evidence, ordinary address names as accessible fallback.
4 EDIT: Same form as Add, all fields prefilled, editable map pin, Street details "Near the old bridge, east gate", small Unsaved changes cue, Save changes/Cancel. No coordinates/degree/range text.
5 VALIDATION: Same form and map as Add. Errors: missing site name, missing Street or landmark details, missing/unusable site location. Summary "Check 3 fields before saving" with links to Site name, Street or landmark details, Site location. Under map show plain "Choose a valid site location on the map." Preserve chosen address fields. Do not display rejected raw coordinate numbers or API field names. Map loading failure uses plain "The map couldn't load. Try again." if shown; never pretend a failed map selected a location.
6 EMPTY DIRECTORY: Same columns as revised directory, no coordinate column. "No supply sites yet", Add supply site, total zero, no fake telemetry.

Map UI is a NEW DESIGN proposal authorized by user revision. Existing API still accepts required latitude/longitude internally; selecting or dragging the map pin supplies these values later when implemented. Addresses do not infer or validate pin coordinates, and no geocoding service is in scope. Use Leaflet-style controls and unobtrusive Geoapify/OpenStreetMap attribution for the agreed map direction. No live map integration or key is required for these static Stitch proposals. Do not show API integration details on product screens.

Keep plain language labels "Site location", "Address", "Street or landmark details". Design preview · Sample records remains visible. No Dispatch, capacity/status/monitoring/weather/audit/concurrency controls. Reuse IBM Plex Sans, 232px sidebar, 56px navbar, calm white sheets, teal brand/near-black primary. No unsupported field metadata/verification claims. At 1440x900 fit full forms and 240–280px map sensibly with scroll if needed; on narrow web screens stack fields, provide labelled menu control, allow usable map and actions without horizontal page overflow. Return all six revised designs.
